statement: For k=25, any counterexample family F of pairwise-disjoint congruence classes of size 25 with all pairwise gcds <= 24: for q in {9,11} (the prime-power thresholds p^E_p landing in (k/3,k/2]), letting I_q = {i : v_p(m_i) >= 1 (q=11) or >= 2 (q=9)}, every pair in I_q has gcd(m_i,m_j) in {q,2q}; splitting I_q = I_q^0 (odd m_i) sqcup J_q (even m_i), every pair within I_q^0 has gcd exactly q and every pair within J_q has gcd exactly 2q, giving injective maps I_q^0 -> Z/qZ and J_q -> Z/2qZ, hence |I_q^0|<=q, |J_q|<=2q, |I_q|<=3q.

For k=25, q in {9,11}: |I_q| <= 3q (27 for q=9, 33 for q=11), which is weaker than the trivial bound |I_q|<=25 and so does not by itself shrink the search domain; the real content of Lemma 4 is the case-split structure (gcd in {q,2q}, not just q) and the resulting cheaper mod-q/mod-2q pairwise disjointness check, not a smaller headcount.

The earlier task p4-proof-9c5676's Lemma 3 (primes p in {13,17,19,23}, i.e. thresholds q=p^E_p > k/2) omitted q=16=2^4, which also exceeds k/2=12.5 for k=25; that gap is not fixed in this task (out of the assigned (k/3,k/2] scope).

Extend the q>k/2 case (currently only proved for odd primes 13,17,19,23) to the composite threshold q=16=2^4 for k=25: show gcd(m_i,m_j) in I_16 is forced to be exactly 16 (single case, since 4*16=64>24 rules out any doubling), giving injectivity mod 16 and |I_16|<=16, a genuine (non-vacuous) extra constraint.

Extend the case-split idea to q<=k/3 (e.g. q=7 for k=25), where up to a 3-way split (gcd in {q,2q,3q}) is needed; work out the resulting partition of I_7 into three homogeneous classes and their injectivity bounds, by analogy with Lemma 4's 2-way split proof here.

Combine Lemma 3 (q in {13,17,19,23}), Lemma 4 here (q in {9,11}), and Sub-lemma A into a single certify-track exhaustiveness certificate for k=25 (finite domain of residues mod each relevant q/2q, pruning rules from all combined injectivity constraints, node counts, rerun) to actually attempt deciding k=25.
